name: External fixator pin locations in the femoral shaft
aliases: femoral shaft Schanz screw safe corridors
corridor: Anterolateral and direct lateral half-pin corridors through vastus lateralis into the femoral diaphysis, keeping medial neurovascular structures protected by the muscular envelope

positioning.text: Position supine or lateral decubitus with the thigh accessible laterally and imaging available; lateral decubitus best exposes the shaft.

surface_landmarks.text: Palpate the tip of the greater trochanter and the lateral border of the femur down the thigh.

incision.text: Make small lateral or anterolateral incisions over the chosen pin sites down to the iliotibial band and vastus lateralis.

superficial_interval.text: Split the fascia lata and pass through or lift vastus lateralis; there is no true internervous plane because this is an intramuscular corridor.

deep_interval.text: In the midshaft place anterolateral pins in the plane between vastus lateralis and rectus femoris, or direct lateral pins through vastus lateralis purchasing both cortices; proximally aim within the lateral face of the greater trochanter and distally use a direct lateral corridor.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, iliotibial band and fascia lata, vastus lateralis, and the lateral femoral cortex.

structures_at_risk.text: The perforating branches of the profunda femoris within vastus lateralis, the femoral vessels medially, and the sciatic nerve posteriorly are at risk; medial cortical perforation endangers the neurovascular structures.

danger_zones.text: Medial cortical perforation and the posterolateral distal femur are danger zones; keep pins anterolateral to direct lateral and avoid a posterolateral distal exit.

retraction_hazards.text: Ligate perforating branches of the profunda femoris that are encountered and avoid levering medially past the far cortex.

exposure.text: Provides safe half-pin corridors along the femoral diaphysis rather than a formal open exposure.

limitations.text: Avoid pins through crush injuries or extensively damaged soft tissue, plan sites for future conversion to nailing or plating, and keep the distal frame off the mattress.

indications.text: Indicated for external fixator half-pin placement in the femoral shaft, commonly for damage-control stabilization.

closure.text: Close each incision loosely around the pin and ensure hemostasis of any divided perforating vessels.

complications.text: Complications include hematoma from perforating vessel injury, neurovascular injury with medial perforation, and pin-tract infection.

procedure_applications.condition: A spanning external fixator is applied to the femur, for example in damage-control orthopedics before nailing

questions.question: Which femoral corridors are safest for external fixator pins?
questions.answer: The anterolateral and direct lateral regions.

questions.question: Why is the anterolateral-to-lateral femur considered safe for pins?
questions.answer: The major neurovascular structures lie medially, protected by the muscular envelope.

questions.question: Which vessels are typically encountered and ligated during lateral vastus lateralis dissection?
questions.answer: The perforating branches of the profunda femoris artery.
